title: Engineering Fibrin-based Tissue Constructs from Myofibroblasts and Application of Constraints and Strain to Induce Cell and Collagen Reorganization
protocol: Isolate cells from the vena saphena magna according to protocol by Schnell et al.
Store isolated cells in liquid nitrogen.
Culture pieces (2 x 2 mm) of vena saphena magna in a six-well plate, using 2 pieces per well.
Thaw cells from one vial and place them into a T75 tissue culture flask.
Add growth medium consisting of Advanced DMEM, FBS, penicillin/streptomycin, and L-glutamax to the flask.
Change the medium every 2-3 days.
Store 0.5 x 10^6 cells in one vial as passage 1 after cells grow confluent approximately after 14 days.
Place HVSCs from one vial into a T175 tissue culture flask and add GM.
Change medium every 2-3 days in the T175 flask until cells grow confluent after approximately 7 days.
Store 3 x 10^6 cells from the confluent flask in one vial at liquid nitrogen for passage 2 storage.
Place cells from one vial into a roller bottle and add GM.
Change medium every 2-3 days in the roller bottle until cells grow confluent after approximately 8 days.
Culture cells up to passage 6.
Do not use cells of a passage higher than passage 9 due to potential changes in cell phenotype.
Mix the elastomer with the curing agent (10:1) to prepare silicone glue for fibrin-based tissue constructs.
Cut 7 x 3 mm rectangular segments of Velcro.
Glue the Velcro into a 6 well culture plate, forming a cross and leaving a squared space of 3 mm between the Velcro strips.
Dry the silicone glue overnight in an oven at 60°C to ensure hardening of the glue.
Sterilize by adding 70% EtOH to the wells and incubate for 30 min.
Rinse the wells and Velcro 3 times with PBS.
Remove all PBS from the wells and Velcro after rinsing.
Put under UV for 30 min and keep sterile until use.
Prepare Tissue Engineering medium (TM) consisting of GM and 130 mg of L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate.
Add 1 mg/ml ε-Amino Caproic Acid (ACA) to the TM.
Dissolve fibrinogen to a concentration of 10 mg actual protein/ml TM supplemented with ACA.
Sterile filter the fibrinogen solution.
Store the filtered fibrinogen solution on ice until use.
Mix thrombin to a concentration of 10 IU/ml TM supplemented with ACA.
Store the mixed thrombin on ice until use.
Trypsinize the cells, resuspend in GM and count.
Use 15 x 10^6 cells/ml for seeding the fibrin-based tissue constructs.
Put 1.5 x 10^6 cells in one centrifuge tube for each gel to be made.
Centrifuge the cells at 350 x g for 7 min and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 50 μl thrombin.
Add 4 μl of blue fluorescent polystyrene microspheres to this suspension.
Put 50 μl of fibrinogen in a vial.
Use a pipette to take up the 50 μl thrombin with cells.
Increase the volume of the pipette to 100 μl.
Pipette the 50 μl solution of thrombin with cells into the vial with fibrinogen to mix the thrombin and fibrinogen.
Take up the 100 μl mixture.
Pipette the gel mixture into and in between the Velcro strips.
Incubate suspensions for 30 min at 37 °C in a humidified 95% air/5% CO2 incubator to allow gelation before adding culture TM with ACA.
Replace TM with ACA every 2-3 days for the first 7 days.
After the first week, replace TM every 2-3 days.
Add 6 ml of TM per well.
On day 12, cells have produced enough collagen for visualization.
Apply static strain by cell traction and compaction directly to the cells.
Cut the tissue construct loose from two Velcro strips in one direction on day 12 to induce unidirectional constraints.
Ensure the construct is stable and sufficient collagen has been deposited before performing the cut.
Apply cyclic strain by applying a vacuum to the bottom of the culture plates with flexible membranes using the Flexcell FX4000T system.
Place the plates on a baseplate, on top of loading posts.
Program a cyclic strain protocol into the controller for the vacuum pump.
Use an intermittent strain of a sine wave with 1 Hz, straining from 0 to 5% strain, for periods of 3 hr, alternated with 3 hr resting periods.
Perform this cyclic strain protocol for 7 days.
Change the uniaxial cyclic strain direction by turning the rectangular posts by 90°.
Label samples with probes that do not interfere with cell viability or collagen formation.
Fluorescently stain the cell cytoplasm and collagen using probes.
Alternatively, use second harmonic generation for visualizing collagen structures with confocal laser scanning microscopy.
Excite at 780 nm and detect between 500-550 nm for autofluorescence visualization of collagen.
Remove culture plates from the setup and incubator during the 3 hr rest period.
Transport cyclically strained samples to a confocal laser scanning microscope.
